claims.statement: An ACMG consensus statement specifically addresses reevaluation and reanalysis of genomic test results as variant knowledge changes.
EHDS is scheduled to make lab-result exchange operational across Member States in 2031 and brings genomic data into later secondary-use rules.
EU IVDR states that software specifically intended for an in-vitro diagnostic medical purpose can itself qualify as an IVD, while general-purpose software does not automatically qualify.

contrary_evidence: The relevant EHDS lab and genomic milestones are years away, so they do not prove near-term demand.
IVDR can turn an automated interpretation claim into a regulated-device obligation, limiting a rapid software launch.

economics.acquisition_route: White-label partnerships with laboratories and genetics clinics rather than consumer advertising
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 100000 active records at 60 PLN annual net revenue could create 6m PLN recurring revenue; at 20% operating margin and 75% ownership, retained cash and a profit-based valuation could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 7
economics.founder_time: 3 hours/day on data and product; clinical interpretation, counselling, and regulatory roles must be delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 60-75% after clinical review, secure hosting, consent operations, and regulatory quality work
economics.payback: Unvalidated: five lab pilots covering 5000 active records could reach operating breakeven in roughly 24 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 60-180 PLN per active record yearly plus 400-1500 PLN for a clinician-reviewed reanalysis
economics.retention_or_repeat: Records remain active for years; reanalysis is episodic and laboratory contracts can renew annually

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consented longitudinal variant records, laboratory integrations, reviewed outcomes, and recontact trust
fingerprint.customer: EU clinical genetics laboratories, private clinics, and patients with prior sequencing results
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: One Polish clinical-lab pilot, genetics clinics, and white-label inclusion with new sequencing tests
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Consent registry, literature/database change detection, lab review queue, audit trail, and patient recontact
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Laboratory or clinic pays per active record and workflow; patient or insurer may pay for a clinician-approved reanalysis
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Variant knowledge changes or a patient remains undiagnosed after an earlier genomic test

founder_fit: Connects neuroscience, genetics, health, and data science
AI can support evidence triage while clinicians retain decisions
B2B laboratory distribution avoids camera-based marketing
Can begin with workflow software before expanding the data network
risks: Incorrect or premature reinterpretation can cause clinical harm
Health and genomic data create exceptional privacy and security exposure
The software may be regulated as an IVD depending on intended purpose

structure.commercial_archetype: Longitudinal record subscription with paid laboratory reanalysis workflow
structure.control_point: Patient consent and the persistent laboratory-to-patient recontact channel for an existing genetic result
structure.critical_dependency: Clinical laboratories must import historical variants and retain responsibility for medically reviewed reinterpretation under IVDR

thesis: Maintain a patient-consented registry of prior clinical genetic findings and give the originating laboratory a governed workflow to re-evaluate, clinically review, and recontact when classifications materially change. Start as lab workflow and consent infrastructure, not direct-to-consumer diagnosis. The durable asset would be the consented longitudinal result graph and recontact relationship.
title: Genomic Result Recontact Registry
uncertainties: Laboratory willingness to accept ongoing recontact duties
Who pays for periodic reanalysis in Poland
Whether sufficient structured historical data can be imported
